• From the Betta albimarginata complex.
  • IUCN Red List: Endangered.
  • Maximum size: 2 inches (about 5 cm).
  • Temperament: somewhat territorial, but can be kept in groups as long as there is enough space.
  • Breeding: mouthbrooder.
Wild caught Betta channoides from Melak. Be sure to have the habitat ready before purchase.
We recommend a pair per 5 gallons (about 19 litres) of water.

• TDS: about 60–100 (tolerates high TDS water but prefers low TDS)
  • pH: 6.0–7.0 (prefers softer water)
  • Temperature: 24–29°C (75–85°F). Prefers cooler temperatures, but higher temperatures induce colouration and breeding behaviour.
Carnivorous. Currently fed live foods such as blackworms, but can be trained to eat frozen and dried foods. Frozen bloodworms and pellets are also fed.

Betta channoides has a more robust body than B. albimarginata and is more red, whereas B. albimarginata can be more of a burgundy to orange colour. The easiest way to tell them apart is that the dorsal fin of B. channoides is all red with no black.
